findings.title: Serving construction escapes close/drain and can leak after rejection
findings.reachable_counterexample: servingFor accepts a current view, then awaits factory verification/listen. Concurrent close/dispose snapshots only #operations, which does not contain this construction, and can close root resources before the continuation. After a listener starts, factory realpath/stat can throw, or service fstat/root validation can throw; neither path closes the new listener. A simple service.close during construction without dispose also permits owner registration/return after closing because #closing/current lease is never rechecked. Parallel servingFor calls both miss #servings and create distinct owners; last registration makes the earlier legitimate returned owner unusable.
findings.test_gap: PF01:924 creates owners sequentially and closes a fully created owner before invoking production; no creation-await close, registration failure or concurrent same-view creation case.
findings.minimum_correction: Admit and track the entire construction before its first await, single-flight by exact held view, recheck closing/lease/record after awaits before registration, and own cleanup of all partially-created listener/folder resources on every failed construction or registration. Add precise creation/close/parallel/failure cases; no extra public module needed.

findings.title: Serving owner closes listener before accepted draw dependencies finish
findings.reachable_counterexample: An already accepted real pageFrame may still need its initial navigation or later asset/iframe requests. Caller can invoke returned serving.close while the draw is awaiting: close immediately stops listener/new connections and drains only currently registered folder HTTP/probe promises, not the producer draw. It can resolve in a gap with no active request while the draw later issues more HTTP. The draw fails or times out because its required origin was torn down. Concurrent repeated close also returns immediately on closed=true instead of sharing original settlement promise.
findings.test_gap: Old B0-2 covers producer browser peer ownership; PF01 only exercises closed-before-draw refusal. Neither covers serving.close during draw with future HTTP dependencies. Service dispose waits its admitted productions, but the public Host-private serving.close path bypasses that wait.
findings.minimum_correction: Stop admitting new productions separately from servicing dependencies of already admitted draws, give serving an actual draw lease/drain ownership, and share a close promise through true settlement before closing listener/root. Assert a delayed future dependency during owner close and repeated-close settlement.

findings.title: A child-page draw can brand an unrelated preexisting film duration
findings.reachable_counterexample: Place a forged finite duration JSON with the real film mtime:size in the issued root, then draw an existing non-film page such as a committed scenes page through the real registered serving. Fixed upstream pageframes.mjs writes film-duration only inside rel===FILM_PAGE and finite duration (pinned file:103), so this draw leaves the forged JSON untouched. The wrapper unconditionally captures any existing duration at665 as an output and activation makes it current by output path; the reader then accepts its full matching identity as witnessed. Likewise a nonfinite film draw can leave a previous duration and have it falsely reissued.
findings.test_gap: PF02:1001 does only one film-poster draw and an equal-bytes/new-inode negative. There is no non-film/preexisting duration negative, change-and-restore duration negative, or actual two-different-frame consecutive draw N8 followed by consumption of both frame triples and latest duration. By-output mapping and per-frame restricted consumption are present statically, but no N8 execution/body proves the requested success.
findings.minimum_correction: Issue authority only for outputs that this exact fixed-producer branch actually wrote; do not adopt prior duration merely because present at POST. Preserve latest per-output authority and old frame triples. Add actual non-film forged duration refusal plus the required two-draw/latest-output positive and tamper negatives.

findings.title: Vendor taint gate misses renamed imports and loader-local calls
findings.reachable_counterexample: Synthetic valid caller: import {createPinnedOpenFilmUpstream as load} from "../../adapters/openfilm/openfilm-upstream.js"; function call(req:IncomingMessage){load(req.url as string)}. imported contains local name load, but known maps exported names, so known.get(load) is undefined and no violation is reported. Namespace import OF.createPinnedOpenFilmUpstream(req.url) is also skipped because only identifier callees are visited. The loader module self-check has no import from itself, so imported is empty and its local openFilmAvailability(requestDerivedRoot) calls are not checked at all. A helper taking root:string and invoking the sink can receive req.url without parameter taint propagation; current helper test only tests pick(req) at a direct sink.
findings.test_gap: Current synthetic request alias and renamed parameter cases do not rename loader import or call through helper into sink. Comment admits cross-file limit, but these bypasses are same-file and beyond that stated limitation. No current production request-controlled vendor path exploit is claimed.
findings.minimum_correction: Resolve local imported aliases/namespaces to original exports, include loader-local entry calls, and follow actual argument-to-helper-parameter data flow or explicitly enforce a smaller audited composition capability boundary. Add these exact counterexamples before relying on the gate; keep fixed argv/pin/shell refusals.

findings.title: Real-media setup cannot overwrite copied opaque fixtures with current ffmpeg argv
findings.reachable_counterexample: Both real-export cases cp SOURCE_FIXTURE recursively, including now-restored17/17/18-byte files, then prepareDiagnosticMedia writes exactly the same output paths. ffmpeg argv has -nostdin and no -y, nor does setup remove only these owned copied files first. Existing output is refused, so the first visual preparation exits before manifest probing, migration, target renders or second edited export. This is a source/CLI control-flow inference, not a claimed run.
findings.test_gap: New actual frames/real AssetRegistry and preserved target900/edit/hash assertions are promising but unreachable from the restored fixture under this setup. Counts/titles or tsc cannot establish LF02.
findings.minimum_correction: Explicitly overwrite or remove only the three owned files in the private copied fixture before fixed bounded generation; preserve canonical opaque bytes and all real render/decode/two-export assertions. Verify audio as well as visual decode; diagnostic remains non-A media.

findings.title: Foreign impact/transaction test uses absent IDs or mismatched request fields
findings.reachable_counterexample: The branch described as an impact of another project never creates such an impact in the same authority; it substitutes imp_of_another_project, an absent ID, and accepts any throw. The transaction branch only substitutes project_id on the original input without creating/selecting an actual transaction belonging to another project. Early missing-row or publication-binding refusal can satisfy both without exercising cross-project CAS/transaction ownership. A defect allowing valid foreign rows could survive these assertions.
findings.test_gap: Tampered stored impact_hash branch is a real DB mutation; expiry delegation and file-scoped fitness registration are present. Those do not establish the two separate actual foreign-authority negatives required by037 LF04.
findings.minimum_correction: Arrange real second-project impact/transaction rows in the same database/authority, prove their existence and foreign ownership before invocation, then assert the intended ownership/CAS refusal and unchanged complete authorities; retain the real hash/rollback and scanner negatives.
